title: TC001-inventory management api should enforce role based access and maintain immutable records
description: Test the inventory management API to ensure it enforces role-based permissions server-side, maintains immutable historical inventory records, and logs all changes for auditability.
code:
import requests
import uuid

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
TIMEOUT = 30
BEARER_TOKEN = "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN_HERE"  # Replace with valid token for respective roles

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {BEARER_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

def test_inventory_management_api_role_enforcement_and_immutable_records():
    # Roles to test with expected permissions
    roles = {
        "Cashier": "token_cashier",
        "Supervisor": "token_supervisor",
        "Manager": "token_manager",
        "SuperAdmin": "token_superadmin"
    }
    
    # Simulated tokens for roles (would be replaced with real tokens in actual tests)
    # Here we test role enforcement by setting tokens accordingly
    # For this test we will:
    # - As Cashier: try to modify inventory (should be forbidden)
    # - As Supervisor: modify inventory (allowed with audit log)
    # - As Cashier or lower try to override pricing or tax settings (forbidden)
    # - Check immutable historical records by attempting to delete or modify past inventory record (should be rejected)
    # - Verify audit logs on changes
    
    # Helper to set authorization header dynamically
    def headers_with_token(token):
        return {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json"
        }
    
    # Step 1: Create a new inventory item as Manager or SuperAdmin for testing immutable record
    # Using SuperAdmin token for creation
    create_token = roles["SuperAdmin"]
    create_headers = headers_with_token(create_token)
    
    product_code = str(uuid.uuid4())
    new_inventory_item = {
        "product_code": product_code,
        "name": "Test Product Immutable",
        "quantity": 100,
        "weight": 1.5,
        "cost_per_unit": 10.0
    }
    
    try:
        # Create inventory item
        r = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory", json=new_inventory_item, headers=create_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 201, f"Failed to create inventory item, status: {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
        created_item = r.json()
        item_id = created_item.get("id")
        assert item_id, "Created inventory item has no id"
        
        # Step 2: Test role-based access enforcement
        # 2a: Cashier tries to update inventory quantity (should be forbidden)
        cashier_token = roles["Cashier"]
        cashier_headers = headers_with_token(cashier_token)
        update_payload = {"quantity": 90}
        r = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory/{item_id}", json=update_payload, headers=cashier_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code in (401, 403), "Cashier should not be able to modify inventory"
        
        # 2b: Supervisor updates inventory quantity (allowed)
        supervisor_token = roles["Supervisor"]
        supervisor_headers = headers_with_token(supervisor_token)
        r = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory/{item_id}", json=update_payload, headers=supervisor_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Supervisor failed to update inventory, status: {r.status_code}, body: {r.text}"
        updated_item = r.json()
        assert updated_item.get("quantity") == 90, "Quantity was not updated by Supervisor"
        
        # 2c: Cashier tries price override (forbidden)
        price_override_payload = {"cost_per_unit": 9.0}
        r = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory/{item_id}", json=price_override_payload, headers=cashier_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code in (401, 403), "Cashier should not be able to override price"
        
        # 2d: Supervisor tries price override within limits (allowed)
        r = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory/{item_id}", json=price_override_payload, headers=supervisor_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, "Supervisor should be able to override price"
        updated_item = r.json()
        assert updated_item.get("cost_per_unit") == 9.0, "Price override failed for Supervisor"
        
        # Step 3: Attempt to modify immutable historical record (simulate by trying to delete the item)
        # Assume API disallows DELETE or makes records immutable
        r = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory/{item_id}", headers=supervisor_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code in (401, 403, 405, 409), "Deletion should be forbidden or rejected for immutable inventory record"
        
        # Step 4: Verify audit logs exist for changes (query audit logs endpoint)
        # Assume audit logs endpoint is /api/admin/audit-logs and accessible to SuperAdmin
        audit_headers = headers_with_token(roles["SuperAdmin"])
        params = {"resource_id": item_id, "resource_type": "inventory"}
        r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/admin/audit-logs", headers=audit_headers, params=params, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, "Failed to retrieve audit logs"
        audit_logs = r.json()
        assert isinstance(audit_logs, list), "Audit logs response should be a list"
        # There should be logs for creation and updates
        event_types = [entry.get("event_type") for entry in audit_logs]
        assert "create" in event_types, "Create event not logged in audit logs"
        assert "update" in event_types, "Update event(s) not logged in audit logs"
        
    finally:
        # Clean up: attempt to delete created inventory item if allowed (or deactivate)
        # If deletion is forbidden, ignore error
        try:
            requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/api/inventory/{item_id}", headers=create_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        except Exception:
            pass

test_inventory_management_api_role_enforcement_and_immutable_records()

title: TC002-credit system api should maintain accurate and auditable customer credit balances
description: Verify that the credit system API accurately manages customer credit lines and balances with immutable transaction records and audit logs for all financial changes.
code:
import requests
import uuid

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
TOKEN = "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN_HERE"  # Replace with a valid token

HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

def test_credit_system_api_maintains_accurate_and_auditable_customer_credit_balances():
    created_customer_credit_id = None
    created_transaction_id = None
    
    try:
        # 1. Create a new customer credit line (POST /api/credit/customers)
        customer_credit_payload = {
            "customerCreditName": f"Test Customer {uuid.uuid4()}",
            "initialCreditLine": 1000.00
        }
        create_credit_response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/customers",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=customer_credit_payload,
            timeout=30
        )
        assert create_credit_response.status_code == 201, f"Failed to create customer credit line: {create_credit_response.text}"
        credit_data = create_credit_response.json()
        created_customer_credit_id = credit_data.get("id")
        assert created_customer_credit_id, "Created customer credit ID missing"
        assert credit_data.get("creditLine") == customer_credit_payload["initialCreditLine"]
        # The balance on creation might be zero or None
        assert credit_data.get("balance") == 0.0 or credit_data.get("balance") is None

        # 2. Add a credit transaction to increase balance (POST /api/credit/transactions)
        transaction_payload = {
            "customerCreditId": created_customer_credit_id,
            "type": "credit",  # Assuming type can be 'credit' or 'debit'
            "amount": 500.00,
            "description": "Initial credit addition for test"
        }
        create_trans_response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/transactions",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=transaction_payload,
            timeout=30
        )
        assert create_trans_response.status_code == 201, f"Failed to create credit transaction: {create_trans_response.text}"
        transaction_data = create_trans_response.json()
        created_transaction_id = transaction_data.get("id")
        assert created_transaction_id, "Created transaction ID missing"
        assert transaction_data.get("amount") == transaction_payload["amount"]
        assert transaction_data.get("type") == transaction_payload["type"]

        # 3. Verify that customer credit balance updated correctly (GET /api/credit/customers/{id})
        get_credit_response = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/customers/{created_customer_credit_id}",
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=30
        )
        assert get_credit_response.status_code == 200, f"Failed to get customer credit details: {get_credit_response.text}"
        credit_details = get_credit_response.json()
        expected_balance = transaction_payload["amount"]
        assert abs(credit_details.get("balance", 0) - expected_balance) < 1e-6, \
            f"Credit balance mismatch: expected {expected_balance}, got {credit_details.get('balance')}"

        # 4. Retrieve transactions and audit logs for customer credit (GET /api/credit/transactions?customerCreditId=)
        get_trans_response = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/transactions",
            headers=HEADERS,
            params={"customerCreditId": created_customer_credit_id},
            timeout=30
        )
        assert get_trans_response.status_code == 200, f"Failed to get transactions: {get_trans_response.text}"
        transactions_list = get_trans_response.json()
        assert any(t.get("id") == created_transaction_id for t in transactions_list), "Transaction record missing"
        # Verify immutability: attempt to modify transaction should fail (PUT /api/credit/transactions/{id})
        update_payload = {
            "amount": 9999.99
        }
        update_trans_response = requests.put(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/transactions/{created_transaction_id}",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=update_payload,
            timeout=30
        )
        # Expect failure, HTTP 4xx or 405 Method Not Allowed
        assert update_trans_response.status_code in (400, 401, 403, 405), \
            "Transaction record is mutable, which violates immutability"

        # 5. Check audit logs for financial changes (GET /api/credit/audit-logs?customerCreditId=)
        get_audit_logs_response = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/audit-logs",
            headers=HEADERS,
            params={"customerCreditId": created_customer_credit_id},
            timeout=30
        )
        assert get_audit_logs_response.status_code == 200, f"Failed to get audit logs: {get_audit_logs_response.text}"
        audit_logs = get_audit_logs_response.json()
        relevant_logs = [log for log in audit_logs if log.get("transaction_id") == created_transaction_id]
        assert len(relevant_logs) > 0, "Audit logs missing for financial transaction"
        for log in relevant_logs:
            assert "timestamp" in log and "action" in log and "performed_by" in log, \
                "Audit log entry missing required fields"

    finally:
        # Cleanup - Delete created transaction and customer credit line if API supports deletion for test purposes
        if created_transaction_id:
            try:
                requests.delete(
                    f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/transactions/{created_transaction_id}",
                    headers=HEADERS,
                    timeout=30
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
        if created_customer_credit_id:
            try:
                requests.delete(
                    f"{BASE_URL}/api/credit/customers/{created_customer_credit_id}",
                    headers=HEADERS,
                    timeout=30
                )
            except Exception:
                pass

test_credit_system_api_maintains_accurate_and_auditable_customer_credit_balances()

title: TC003-ai insights api should generate accurate business analytics and insights
description: Test the AI insights API to ensure it generates accurate and reproducible business insights and analytics based on current and historical data.
code:
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
AI_INSIGHTS_ENDPOINT = f"{BASE_URL}/api/ai/insights"
TOKEN = "your_bearer_token_here"
HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}
TIMEOUT = 30

def test_ai_insights_api_should_generate_accurate_business_analytics_and_insights():
    """Test the AI insights API to ensure it generates accurate and reproducible business insights and analytics based on current and historical data."""
    # Example payload simulating a request for business insights with some dummy data references
    request_payload = {
        "queryPeriod": {
            "startDate": "2024-01-01",
            "endDate": "2024-12-31"
        },
        "metrics": ["revenue", "profit", "customerRetention", "inventoryTurnover"],
        "historicalComparison": True,
        "businessUnits": ["Sales", "Inventory", "CustomerService"]
    }

    try:
        response = requests.post(
            AI_INSIGHTS_ENDPOINT,
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=request_payload,
            timeout=TIMEOUT
        )
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"Request to AI insights API failed: {e}"

    # Assert HTTP status code indicates success
    assert response.status_code == 200, f"Expected status code 200, got {response.status_code}"

    try:
        data = response.json()
    except ValueError:
        assert False, "Response is not valid JSON"

    # Validate structure of the response
    # Expecting keys such as 'insights', 'analytics', 'generatedAt', 'queryPeriod'
    assert "insights" in data, "'insights' key missing from response"
    assert isinstance(data["insights"], list), "'insights' should be a list"

    assert "analytics" in data, "'analytics' key missing from response"
    assert isinstance(data["analytics"], dict), "'analytics' should be a dictionary"

    assert "generatedAt" in data, "'generatedAt' key missing from response"

    assert "queryPeriod" in data, "'queryPeriod' key missing from response"
    qp = data["queryPeriod"]
    assert "startDate" in qp and "endDate" in qp, "'startDate' or 'endDate' missing in 'queryPeriod'"

    # Basic sanity checks on insights content 
    for insight in data["insights"]:
        assert isinstance(insight, dict), "Each insight should be a dictionary"
        assert "title" in insight and isinstance(insight["title"], str), "Insight missing 'title' or not a string"
        assert "description" in insight and isinstance(insight["description"], str), "Insight missing 'description' or not a string"
        # Optionally check for evidence or confidence score if present
        if "confidenceScore" in insight:
            score = insight["confidenceScore"]
            assert isinstance(score, (int, float)) and 0 <= score <= 1, "Invalid 'confidenceScore' in insight"

    # Validate analytics fields for expected metrics keys
    expected_metrics = set(request_payload["metrics"])
    actual_metrics = set(data["analytics"].keys())
    missing_metrics = expected_metrics - actual_metrics
    assert not missing_metrics, f"Expected metrics missing in analytics: {missing_metrics}"

    # Check reproducibility: Call API second time with same payload and compare results
    try:
        response_2 = requests.post(
            AI_INSIGHTS_ENDPOINT,
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=request_payload,
            timeout=TIMEOUT
        )
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"Second request to AI insights API failed: {e}"

    assert response_2.status_code == 200, f"Second request status code not 200, got {response_2.status_code}"

    try:
        data_2 = response_2.json()
    except ValueError:
        assert False, "Second response is not valid JSON"

    # Basic check: The insights and analytics should match for reproducibility
    assert data["insights"] == data_2["insights"], "Insights differ between repeated requests"
    assert data["analytics"] == data_2["analytics"], "Analytics differ between repeated requests"

test_ai_insights_api_should_generate_accurate_business_analytics_and_insights()

import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
TOKEN = "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN_HERE"  # Replace with a valid super admin bearer token

HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

def test_admin_management_api_access_control_and_audit_logs():
    # Create a new user as Super Admin
    user_payload = {
        "username": "testuser_tc004",
        "email": "testuser_tc004@example.com",
        "role": "Manager"
    }
    user_id = None
    try:
        # Create user endpoint
        create_user_resp = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/admin/user",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=user_payload,
            timeout=30
        )
        assert create_user_resp.status_code == 201, f"User creation failed: {create_user_resp.text}"
        user_data = create_user_resp.json()
        user_id = user_data.get("id")
        assert user_id, "User ID not returned on creation"

        # Verify role enforcement: try to perform a permission-restricted admin action as the created user (simulate access)

        # Attempt to change permissions as the created user (should fail)
        # Simulate this by token swap or assume /api/admin/permissions endpoint expects super admin
        # For this test, confirm that only super admin can update permissions

        # We simulate permission update with wrong role token => here we just confirm super admin can do it

        # Update user role to 'Supervisor' as Super Admin
        update_payload = {
            "role": "Supervisor"
        }
        update_resp = requests.put(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/admin/users/{user_id}",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=update_payload,
            timeout=30
        )
        assert update_resp.status_code == 200, f"User role update failed: {update_resp.text}"
        updated_user = update_resp.json()
        assert updated_user.get("role") == "Supervisor", "User role not updated correctly"

        # Fetch audit logs filtered by user creation and update actions
        audit_resp = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/admin/audit-logs",
            headers=HEADERS,
            params={"userId": user_id},
            timeout=30
        )
        assert audit_resp.status_code == 200, f"Failed to fetch audit logs: {audit_resp.text}"
        audit_logs = audit_resp.json()
        assert isinstance(audit_logs, list), "Audit logs response is not a list"
        # There should be at least two audit log entries: creation and update
        creation_logged = any(
            log.get("action") == "create_user" and log.get("userId") == user_id for log in audit_logs
        )
        update_logged = any(
            log.get("action") == "update_user_role" and log.get("userId") == user_id for log in audit_logs
        )
        assert creation_logged, "User creation action not logged in audit logs"
        assert update_logged, "User role update action not logged in audit logs"

        # Verify audit logs are append-only: attempt to delete an audit log should fail (simulate with DELETE)
        if audit_logs:
            audit_log_id = audit_logs[0].get("id")
            if audit_log_id:
                del_resp = requests.delete(
                    f"{BASE_URL}/api/admin/audit-logs/{audit_log_id}",
                    headers=HEADERS,
                    timeout=30
                )
                assert del_resp.status_code in (403, 405, 400), "Audit logs should be append-only and deletion must be forbidden"

    finally:
        # Cleanup: delete the created user
        if user_id:
            del_user_resp = requests.delete(
                f"{BASE_URL}/api/admin/users/{user_id}",
                headers=HEADERS,
                timeout=30
            )
            # Deletion success code can be 200 or 204; also handle error silently here
            assert del_user_resp.status_code in (200, 204), f"Cleanup user deletion failed: {del_user_resp.text}"

title: TC005-team management api should enforce role based permissions and support team member management
description: Test the team management API to ensure it enforces role-based permissions, supports adding, updating, and removing team members, and logs all permission changes.
code:
import requests
import uuid

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
TIMEOUT = 30
AUTH_TOKEN = "your_bearer_token_here"  # Replace with valid token

HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

def test_team_management_role_based_permissions():
    team_member_id = None
    try:
        # 1. Add a new team member with role 'Cashier'
        add_payload = {
            "name": "Test User",
            "email": f"testuser_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com",
            "role": "Cashier"
        }
        add_resp = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=add_payload,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert add_resp.status_code == 201, f"Failed to add team member: {add_resp.text}"
        added_member = add_resp.json()
        team_member_id = added_member.get("id")
        assert team_member_id is not None, "Added team member ID missing"

        # 2. Verify role-based permission enforcement: try an unauthorized action as Cashier
        # Assume "update role" is restricted to Manager or above.
        update_payload_unauth = {"role": "Manager"}
        update_resp_unauth = requests.put(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}/role",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=update_payload_unauth,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        # Expecting error status due to insufficient permission
        assert update_resp_unauth.status_code in (403, 401), \
            "Role-based permission not enforced on unauthorized role update"

        # 3. Update team member role as authorized user
        # For this test, we assume the AUTH_TOKEN belongs to a user with proper rights.
        # To simulate, we override the token temporarily if needed.
        # Here we retry with the same token assuming it has rights.
        update_payload_auth = {"role": "Supervisor"}
        update_resp_auth = requests.put(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}/role",
            headers=HEADERS,
            json=update_payload_auth,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert update_resp_auth.status_code == 200, f"Failed to update role: {update_resp_auth.text}"
        updated_member = update_resp_auth.json()
        assert updated_member.get("role") == "Supervisor", "Team member role not updated correctly"

        # 4. Get audit logs related to permission changes for the member
        audit_resp = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}/audit-logs",
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert audit_resp.status_code == 200, f"Failed to fetch audit logs: {audit_resp.text}"
        audit_logs = audit_resp.json()
        assert isinstance(audit_logs, list), "Audit logs should be a list"
        # Check that audit logs contain the role update action
        role_change_logged = any(
            log.get("action") == "role_update" and log.get("member_id") == team_member_id
            for log in audit_logs
        )
        assert role_change_logged, "Role update action not logged in audit logs"

        # 5. Remove the team member
        del_resp = requests.delete(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}",
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert del_resp.status_code == 204, f"Failed to delete team member: {del_resp.text}"

        # 6. Verify team member no longer exists
        get_resp = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}",
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert get_resp.status_code == 404, "Deleted team member still accessible"

        # 7. Verify audit log contains the deletion action
        audit_after_del_resp = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}/audit-logs",
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        # This might return 404 or valid logs depending on implementation; accept both but check logs if exists
        if audit_after_del_resp.status_code == 200:
            logs_after_del = audit_after_del_resp.json()
            deletion_logged = any(
                log.get("action") == "member_deletion" and log.get("member_id") == team_member_id
                for log in logs_after_del
            )
            assert deletion_logged, "Member deletion not logged in audit logs"
        else:
            assert audit_after_del_resp.status_code in (404, 410), \
                f"Unexpected status fetching audit logs after deletion: {audit_after_del_resp.status_code}"

    finally:
        # Cleanup: attempt to delete the team member if still exists
        if team_member_id is not None:
            try:
                requests.delete(
                    f"{BASE_URL}/api/team/members/{team_member_id}",
                    headers=HEADERS,
                    timeout=TIMEOUT,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass

import requests
import uuid

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001"
TOKEN = "YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN_HERE"  # Replace with a valid bearer token

HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

timeout = 30

def test_notifications_api_alerts_and_user_management():
    notification_id = None
    try:
        # 1. Create a user notification preference
        user_pref_payload = {
            "userId": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "preferences": {
                "emailAlerts": True,
                "pushAlerts": True,
                "smsAlerts": False
            }
        }
        resp = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/notifications/preferences",
            json=user_pref_payload,
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=timeout
        )
        assert resp.status_code == 201, f"Create prefs failed: {resp.text}"
        created_prefs = resp.json()
        assert created_prefs["userId"] == user_pref_payload["userId"]
        assert created_prefs["preferences"]["emailAlerts"] is True

        user_id = created_prefs["userId"]

        # 2. Deliver an alert notification for the user
        alert_payload = {
            "userId": user_id,
            "type": "ALERT",
            "message": "Your account will undergo scheduled maintenance at midnight.",
            "metadata": {
                "severity": "info"
            }
        }
        resp = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/notifications/alerts",
            json=alert_payload,
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=timeout
        )
        assert resp.status_code == 201, f"Alert delivery failed: {resp.text}"
        alert = resp.json()
        notification_id = alert.get("notificationId")
        assert notification_id is not None
        assert alert["userId"] == user_id
        assert alert["message"] == alert_payload["message"]

        # 3. Fetch user notification preferences to verify they are stored correctly
        resp = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/notifications/preferences/{user_id}",
            headers=HEADERS,
            timeout=timeout
        )
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Fetch prefs failed: {resp.text}"
        prefs = resp.json()
        assert prefs["userId"] == user_id
        assert prefs["preferences"]["emailAlerts"] is True

        resp = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api/notifications/auditlogs",

            timeout=timeout
        )
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Fetch audit logs failed: {resp.text}"
        logs = resp.json()
        # Confirm the notification event is logged

        assert len(notifications_logged) > 0, "Notification event not found in audit logs"

    finally:
        # Cleanup: delete the created notification if possible
        if notification_id:
            requests.delete(
                f"{BASE_URL}/api/notifications/alerts/{notification_id}",
                headers=HEADERS,
                timeout=timeout
            )
        # Cleanup: delete the user notification preferences
        if 'user_id' in locals():
            requests.delete(
                f"{BASE_URL}/api/notifications/preferences/{user_id}",
                headers=HEADERS,
                timeout=timeout
            )
